assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 40,000 rps at peak. 72% map-tile fetches (a single map view pulls a dozen tiles), 12% geocode/places search, 10% route requests, 6% anonymised live-traffic probes uploaded by client devices.

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: Tile CDN hit-rate 95%: tiles are immutable per zoom/version, which makes them the most cacheable objects in any consumer product. Only 5% of tile requests reach the origin store.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Route cache hit-rate 60% and geocode cache hit-rate 50%. Routes repeat far more than intuition suggests (commutes, popular POI pairs) but only at a coarse origin/destination granularity, so 60% assumes snapping to a routing-cell grid rather than exact coordinates.

assumptions.subject: route
assumptions.statement: A routing query is the most expensive request in the system by two orders of magnitude: ~250 rps per instance and 45 ms of service time for a contraction-hierarchies query over a continental graph with alternatives. Nine instances carry 1,600 rps. This is why route caching exists at all.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: PostGIS at ~4,000 rps for POI lookup and reverse geocoding. Spatial index scans are far heavier than point lookups, which is why this is a third of the throughput assumed for a plain OLTP primary in other designs.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Edge tile delivery is roughly 1.8 PB/month (28,800 tile req/s at ~25 KB) and is NOT priced below: like any CDN contract it is bought at rates well under the model's flat $0.09/GB internet rate, and pricing it flat would overstate the bill badly. What IS priced is the metered origin fill — 5% of that volume, ~91 TB/month — plus 200 TB of pre-rendered tile storage.

assumptions.subject: scope
assumptions.statement: SINGLE REGION, by Keystone's v1 scope freeze. A real mapping product is multi-region with geo-routed traffic, and latency to the nearest region is a first-order part of its design. The engine has no multi-region model, so treat this as one region's worth of capacity and multiply, rather than as a global design.

assumptions.subject: q
assumptions.statement: Live traffic probes (2,400/s) flow into a 3-broker bus and are aggregated into the live-speed cache. The aggregation job that turns raw probes into road-segment speeds is a stream/batch workload and is not modelled; only the ingest hop is.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: Turn-by-turn navigation sessions are long-lived, stateful and push-based (a device holds a session and receives reroutes). The engine models independent request arrivals only, so navigation is represented here as the route requests that start and re-plan a trip, not as concurrent sessions.

_library.summary: Consumer mapping stack: CDN-cached map tiles plus geocoding, an expensive routing engine and live-traffic probe ingest behind one API.
